sense: new, not copied; of a person, inventive

evidence: Cic. Rep. 1.13: nova et ā nōbīs inventa ratiō
Cic. Rep. 1.21: nihil novī vōbīs adferam, neque quod ā mē sit cōgitātum aut inventum
terms.comment: An original idea is new and one’s own: novum et ā mē inventum, new and found by me. See new.

evidence: Cic. Caecin. 36: novum est, nōn dīcō inūsitātum, vērum omnīnō inaudītum
terms.comment: A favourite word of Cicero’s (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: of a person: inventive, clever, gifted

evidence: Apul. M. 11.2: Cerēs … frūgum parēns orīginālis (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Late Latin, and only of what comes first or from the source (see original: first); it never meant new or inventive.

phrases.latin: Nūllum est jam dictum quod nōn dictum sit prius.
phrases.english: Nothing is said now that has not been said before.

phrases.latin: Nihil novī vōbīs adferam, neque quod ā mē sit cōgitātum aut inventum
phrases.english: I shall bring you nothing new, nothing thought out or discovered by me

phrases.latin: similem esse tē volō quōmodo fīlium, nōn quōmodo imāginem: imāgō rēs mortua est
phrases.english: I want you to resemble your model as a son does, not as a portrait does: a portrait is a dead thing

sources: Lewis & Short: novus · Lewis & Short: inauditus · Lewis & Short: ingeniosus · Lewis & Short: originalis
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 32.
